explanation: Searched Mathlib for the finite (co)product/(co)limit reflection classes (ReflectsFiniteProducts, ReflectsFiniteCoproducts, ReflectsFiniteLimits, ReflectsFiniteColimits) and for all opposite-functor transport lemmas about them (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Limits/Preserves/Opposites.lean, Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Limits/Preserves/Finite.lean). The only related Mathlib statements are: (a) the sibling lemmas in the same file (reflectsFiniteProducts_rightOp and the op/leftOp/unop variants, and the `_of_` directions), which are different statements (swapped direction or different functor shape), and (b) reflectsFiniteColimits_rightOp / reflectsLimits_rightOp / reflectsColimits_rightOp etc., which concern the stronger, non-finite class ReflectsFiniteColimits/ReflectsLimits/ReflectsColimits rather than ReflectsFiniteProducts. No Mathlib declaration states that `F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D` reflecting finite products makes `F.rightOp` reflect finite coproducts; deriving it would require a multi-step argument via `ReflectsColimitsOfShape` and `Discrete.opposite` equivalences, so neither duplicate nor a one-declaration special case exists.
